description.narrative:
This contract is the support to STEG envisaged in the context of the

ELMED project and the infrastructure aspects related to the Owner¿s

Engineering. In particular:

¿ Project Oversight and Coordination: Recognizing the

substantial institutional capacity risks associated with

coordinating a complex interconnector involving HVDC

technology and submarine cable, the OE would play a critical

role in assisting STEG in the administration and supervision

of the design and construction of the Project. This supervision

extends to STEG's engagement with Terna and multiple

international financial institutions (IFIs), which are parallel

financiers of the project. The OE's oversight would help

navigate these intricate relationships and ensure effective

project coordination. Given the intricate nature of these

interactions, a well-defined Contract Management Plan

prepared by the OE is essential to establish clear roles,

responsibilities, communication channels, key performance

indicators, milestones, and reporting mechanisms.

¿ Technical Expertise: Considering STEG's limited experience

with HVDC technology, submarine cable interconnectors and

advanced dispatch center technologies, the OE's technical

expertise becomes crucial.

¿ Overall contract management support. The Consultant shall

administer the contracts, taking due regard of all relevant

circumstances. The OE shall act proactively, and in addition

provide all necessary warning and reminders to the

Contractors and the Employer to ensure timely and smooth

implementation of the Project and prevent claims by the

Contractor/s in response to the Contractor/s¿ or the

Employer¿s requests.

¿ Quality Assurance and Quality Control: Given the

institutional capacity risks, rigorous quality assurance and

control mechanisms become even more essential. The OE

will conduct thorough reviews of design submissions, factory

tests, and installation procedures to safeguard project quality

and compliance.

¿ Testing and Commissioning: OE's role in testing and

commissioning gains added significance as a mean of

mitigating institutional capacity risks. By ensuring thorough

testing and verification of the submarine cable's performance

and associated infrastructure such as the converter stations

and the dispatch center, the consultant contributes to the

project's operational success and sustainability.
